name: Sunspel
why: Fine-cotton tees, underwear and knitwear, including the Riviera mesh polo, made in England.
origin: Founded in Nottingham in 1860 by Thomas Hill.

notes.cotton: Supima traceable to a single California farm, knitted into the 1950s Riviera mesh
notes.racquet: The Riviera mesh and a long British club lineage rather than any tennis program. It reads courtside through association and cloth, not through kit.
notes.whitet: The Riviera and the classic tee are the house; loopback and long-staple cotton since 1860.

notes.briish: Made in Long Eaton since 1860; the Riviera polo and the English tee are the brand.
notes.craft: Sunspel genuinely owns and documents its Long Eaton factory (since 1937), and the Classic T-shirt PDP says it is made there. But its own Factories page lists Long Eaton as making T-shirts only, with every other category made by partner factories, and 7 of 8 sampled PDPs say Made in Portugal. Owned making of a core category, not the whole range: a 4 on the rubric.

craft_evidence.owned_d: Own factory at Long Eaton, England, on site since 1937 (a converted lace mill); brand's Factories page lists it as the one Sunspel-owned factory and says it makes luxury T-shirts; journal article describes the 12-step handmaking of the Classic T-shirt there, with photographs. All other categories (polos, sweats, knitwear, shirts, jackets, underwear, shoes) are listed as made by partner factories, mostly in Portugal.
craft_evidence.countries: Portugal 7/8, England 1/8 (sample of 8 PDPs on us.sunspel.com: Classic T-shirt, Riviera T-shirt, Riviera polo, merino crew, cashmere polo, loopback sweatshirt, flannel shirt, suede Harrington). Only the Classic T-shirt was England; even the Riviera T-shirt is Portugal. A 'Made in Britain' collection exists (Classic T-shirts, some Scottish knitwear, accessories).
